title: Failed Execution excludes unknown outcomes and never counts a blind resend as a duplicate
risk: An unknown outcome after a dropped response is filed as a failure, or a blind resend is hidden as a vendor artifact, so the failure rate and the zero-duplicate invariant are both wrong at the same time.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
The dataset separates failed executions, unknown outcomes and duplicate executions into three counters that must not be merged.
A variant injects one unknown outcome and one blind resend whose effect already occurred, so the case can prove the buckets stay distinct.

expected.unknown_outcome_bucket: separate counter, excluded from both failure and success

steps.action: Compute Failed Execution over the dataset
steps.expected: The rate is 0.3% from three failed executions out of one thousand, and unknown outcomes are reported in their own counter rather than inside the failure numerator.

steps.action: Inject the unknown outcome and the blind resend
steps.expected: The unknown counter increments once, the failure numerator is unchanged, and the blind resend resolves through reconciliation without creating a second external effect.

steps.action: Read the duplicate-execution invariant after the blind resend
steps.expected: The invariant stays exactly 0 because no second effect occurred, and the extra attempt is visible as an attempt rather than as a duplicate.

steps.action: Attempt to publish the failure threshold as an approved limit
steps.expected: The publication is refused: the threshold remains a proposed design target awaiting the ASM-002 baseline, while the zero-duplicate invariant continues to apply immediately.

assertions: Failed Execution counts failed or errored executions only; unknown outcomes live in their own bucket and are excluded from both the failure and the success numerators.
The duplicate-execution invariant is unaffected by a retry that produced no second effect, and by a blind resend that was reconciled before dispatch.
A retry that later succeeds does not retroactively remove the earlier failure record.
The failure threshold is labelled as an unapproved design target, while the zero-duplicate invariant is applied immediately without waiting for a baseline.
forbidden: Counting an unknown outcome as a failure to make the failure rate look conservative.
Hiding a blind resend so a second effect is never investigated.
Removing an earlier failure record after a successful retry.
evidence: Execution ledger with the three counters and the retry links.
Unknown-outcome and reconciliation records for the injected variant.
Invariant evaluation rows before and after the blind resend.
cleanup: Delete gov- execution, unknown-outcome and evaluation rows after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
